ex: Well, geomagnetic activity, the natural variations in Earth's magnetic field, it fluctuates in 11-year cycles.
地磁活動，也就是地球磁場的自然變化，其波動週期是 11 年。
words.en: relating to the earth's magnetic field

words.zh: 沼澤的，泥濘的
ex: Wetlands are areas of marshy, swampy land, areas where water covers the soil, or is present either at or near the surface of the soil for a large part of the year.
濕地是多沼澤、濕軟的地帶，在一年中大部分時間內，這些區域要麼被水淹沒，要麼水位處於或接近地表。
words.en: soft, wet land

words.zh: n. 1. 小球，團粒 2. 小子彈；v. 1. 使成彈丸狀 2. 用子彈打
ex: What happens is that small (millimeter-to centimeter-size) pellets of ice form in the cold upper regions of the cloud.
所發生的情況就是微小的冰粒（從幾毫米到幾釐米大小）會在雲層寒冷的上層區域形成。
words.en: a small hard ball of something

words.zh: 顆粒，細粒
ex: With additional time, pressure and refrozen meltwater from above, the small firn granules become larger, interlocked crystals of blue glacial ice.
隨著時間的推移，在持續壓力，以及那些位於上方的融雪重新結冰的作用下，那些較小的粒雪顆粒就會變成更大的、互相連結的藍色冰川晶體。
words.en: a very small piece of something

words.zh: n. 釉，釉料；v. 1. 上釉，使光亮 2. 裝玻璃
ex: Furthermore, the designs were covered with "desert varnish," a glaze that develops on rock surfaces over thousands of years of exposure to the elements.
此外，這些圖案被「沙漠漆」所覆蓋，這種沙漠漆是經過數千年暴露於自然條件下後在岩石表面形成的一種釉料。
words.en: a thin shiny coat on pottery; to cover with a thin layer

words.zh: 無機的，無生物的
ex: A mineral is a naturally occurring solid formed by inorganic processes.
礦物是一種通過無機過程形成的天然固態物質。
words.en: not made of living things

words.zh: 診斷的，判斷的
words.mnem: dia- (=through) + gnos (=know) + -tic → 通過……而得知 → 診斷的，判斷的
ex: Although color is an obvious feature of a mineral, it is often an unreliable diagnostic property.
儘管顏色是礦物的一個顯著特徵，但它往往是一種不可靠的鑒定屬性。
words.en: used to identify a disease or a problem

words.zh: 即將發生的，迫在眉睫的
words.mnem: im- (=on) + pend (=hang) + -ing → 懸在上面的 → 即將發生的，迫在眉睫的
ex: Before a volcano erupts, hot magma rises toward the surface, so any local manifestation of increasing heat may signal an impending event.
在火山噴發之前，熾熱的岩漿會向地表上升，因此任何局部升溫跡象都可能預示著噴發即將發生。
words.en: about to happen

words.zh: 1. 降水（包括雨、雪等）2. 沉澱，澱析
words.mnem: pre- (=before) + cipit (=head) + -ation → 一頭栽下 →（引申義）降水
ex: Climate pertains to the enduring patterns of temperature, humidity, wind, and precipitation in a specific geographical region or area over time.
氣候指的是特定地理區域或地區內，在一段較長時間內呈現出的氣溫、濕度、風及降水的長期穩定模式。
deriv: precipitate v. 使突然發生 n. 沉澱物 a. 魯莽的
words.en: rain, snow or hail; the process of becoming solid in a liquid

words.zh: 有節奏（或規律）的，節奏分明的
ex: Eruptions are often preceded by a distinctive pattern of earthquake activity called harmonic tremors, a continuous rhythmic rumbling.
火山噴發之前通常會出現一種被稱為諧波震顫的獨特地震活動模式，即持續且有規律的隆隆震動。
words.en: having a regular repeated pattern of sounds or movements

words.zh: v. [ˈɔːrient] 1. 確定方位 2. 熟悉，適應；n. [ˈɔːriənt] 東方國家
words.mnem: ori (=rise) + -ent → 太陽升起的地方 → 東方 → 確定方位
ex: Earth is surrounded by a magnetic field and we know that every magnet has a North and a South Pole and things get oriented toward those poles.
地球被磁場環繞，而我們知道，每塊磁體都有南極和北極，並且物體會因此指向磁極的方向。
deriv: oriental a. 東方人的，東方的
orientation n. 目標；態度；培訓
words.en: to find your position; to adapt to a new situation

words.zh: 1. 分裂 2. 分歧，差異 3. 乳溝
ex: The tendency of a mineral to break along planes of weak bonding is called cleavage.
礦物沿弱鍵平面斷裂的傾向稱為解理。
words.en: a split or division; the tendency of a mineral to split along planes

words.zh: 岩漿
ex: Volcanoes are the landforms created when molten rock, or magma, escapes from vents in the Earth's surface and then solidifies around these vents.
火山是一種地貌形態，當熔融的岩石，即岩漿，從地球表面的火山口噴出，隨後在這些火山口周圍凝固時，就形成了火山。
words.en: hot liquid rock under the earth's surface

words.zh: 使受害，使受苦
ex: It is not uncommon for lack of rain and too much rain simultaneously to victimize two or more parts of China.
在中國，部分地區干旱少雨，而同時另一些地區暴雨成災，這種情況並不少見。
words.en: to treat someone unfairly

words.zh: 1. 火一般的，火的 2. 暴躁的，易怒的
ex: It was pretty much covered in magma, with really fiery conditions, like volcanoes.
它幾乎完全被岩漿覆蓋，環境熾熱非常，就像在火山附近一樣。
words.en: burning or bright like fire; passionate

words.zh: 1. 泥土的 2. 粗俗的，庸俗的，不文雅的
ex: Luster is a good guide to the identity of glassy and metallic minerals, but not those that have dull or earthy appearance.
光澤是鑒別玻璃質和金屬礦物的重要依據，但對於那些外觀暗淡或土狀的礦物來說，光澤並不是有效的鑒別方法。
words.en: like soil; direct and simple in a way that may be rude

words.zh: 收縮，縮小
words.mnem: con- (=together) + tract (=draw) + -ion → 收縮，縮小
ex: With continued contraction came continued deformation, but with the continents and oceans always in the same relative positions.
隨著持續收縮，變形也持續發生，但大陸和海洋的相對位置始終保持不變。
deriv: contract n. 合同，合約 v.（使）收縮，縮小；感染（疾病）；訂合同
words.en: the process of becoming smaller

words.zh: n. 1. 成分，構成要素 2. 選民，選舉人；a. 組成的，構成的
words.mnem: con- (=together) + stitu (=stand) + -ent → 站在一起 → 成分，構成要素
ex: On Earth it is a minor constituent.
在地球上，它是一種次要成分。
words.en: one of the parts that form something

words.zh: 沉積的，沉積形成的
words.mnem: sed (=sit) + i + -ment + -ary → 坐在底部的 → 沉積的
ex: These preserved remains of ancient organisms are typically found in sedimentary rocks.
這些保存完好的古代生物遺骸，通常存在於沉積岩中。
deriv: sediment n. 沉澱物；沉積物
words.en: formed from material that settled at the bottom of water

words.zh: 1. 地震的，地震引起的 2. 重大的，影響深遠的
words.mnem: seism (=shake) + -ic → 晃動的 → 地震的
ex: Seismic waves—energy waves produced by earthquakes—permit scientists to determine the location, thickness, and properties of Earth's internal zones.
地震波——由地震產生的能量波——使科學家能夠確定地球內部區域的位置、厚度和特性。
words.en: relating to earthquakes

words.zh: a. 有差別的，視差別而定的；n. 差別
words.mnem: dif- (=apart) + fer (=carry) + -ent + -ial → 分開拿 → 有差別的
ex: Solar energy reaching Earth is responsible for differential heating of the atmosphere and thus air circulation as wind.
到達地球的太陽能造成了大氣的不均衡受熱，進而形成風這種空氣環流。
deriv: differentiate v. 區別；使有差別
words.en: showing a difference; a difference between two things

words.zh: 彈性，彈力
ex: The change in velocity that occurs as body waves invade rocks of different elasticity results in a bending or refraction of the wave.
當體波進入具有不同彈性的岩石時，所發生的速度變化會導致波的彎曲或折射。
deriv: elastic a. 有彈性的，有彈力的；可改變的，靈活的 n. 橡皮圈（或帶），鬆緊帶
words.en: the quality of being able to stretch and return to shape

words.zh: 1. 高出地面的 2. 偏高的 3. 高尚的
words.mnem: e- (=up) + lev (=raise) + -ated → 高出地面的
ex: The collapsed portions formed the ocean basins; the remaining elevated portions formed the continents.
塌陷的部分形成了海洋盆地，其餘隆起的部分形成了大陸。
deriv: elevate v. 抬起；提升，提拔
elevation n. 高度；提升；高地
words.en: raised above a level

words.zh: 不滲漏的，透不過的
words.mnem: im- (=not) + per- (=through) + me (=glide) + -able → 不滲漏的，透不過的
ex: In addition, because the city surface is impermeable, the runoff of water following a rain is rapid, resulting in a severe reduction in the evaporation rate.
此外，由於城市地表不透水，降雨後的徑流迅速，導致蒸發率大幅降低。
words.en: not allowing liquid to pass through

words.zh: v. 1. 使不相信，使懷疑 2. 損害……的名譽，使丟臉；n. 名譽喪失，信譽喪失
words.mnem: dis- (=apart) + cred (=believe) + -it → 使不相信
ex: The research of D. M. Barringer and Gene Shoemaker provided solid evidence supporting impact formation and was a major factor in discrediting the volcanic creation theory.
D. M. Barringer 和 Gene Shoemaker 的研究為撞擊成因說提供了確鑿證據，也是否定火山成因說的一個關鍵因素。
deriv: discreditable a. 不光彩的，有損尊嚴的
words.en: to harm the reputation of someone or something

words.zh: v. [trəˈvɜːrs] 橫過，穿過；n. [ˈtrævɜːrs] 橫過，橫越
words.mnem: tra- (=across) + vers (=turn) + -e → 橫過，穿過
ex: Their energy is less rapidly scattered into the large volumes of rock traversed by body waves.
它們的能量在被體波穿過的大量岩石中擴散得較為緩慢。
words.en: to cross something

words.zh: v. 1. 猛推 2. 刺，戳；n. 1. 猛推 2. 要點，要旨
ex: They were thrust up either by the plowing of the continents through the sima, as in the case of the Andes, or...
山脈的隆起，要麼是由於硅鎂層陸塊的推擠而成，就像安第斯山脈；要麼是……
words.en: to push something forcefully; the main point of something

words.zh: 沙漠化
ex: Second, plans for fighting desertification involve asking local people to install and maintain the devices.
第二，防治荒漠化的計劃需要當地民眾安裝並維護這些設備。
deriv: desert n. 沙漠 v. 離棄；拋棄
words.en: the process by which land becomes desert

words.zh: 1. 不規律的，不均勻的 2. 不平坦的 3. 不公平的 4. 實力懸殊的 5. 質量不穩定的
ex: Some minerals exhibit poor cleavage because they tend to break in an uneven manner.
有些礦物的解理性較差，因為它們容易發生不均勻斷裂。
words.en: not smooth or equal

words.zh: 誤解，錯誤想法
ex: The reason for this misconception is that most crystals do not exhibit their crystal form.
這種誤解的原因在於，大多數晶體並不顯現其晶體形態。
words.en: a wrong idea about something

words.zh: n. 蛇紋石；a. 蜿蜒的
ex: So-called serpentine soils, for example, are deficient in calcium, and only plants able to tolerate low levels of this mineral can survive.
比如，所謂的蛇紋岩土壤缺乏鈣質，因而只有那些對這種礦物質含量要求不高的植物才能在此土壤中存活。
words.en: winding like a snake; a green mineral

words.zh: 1. 溫帶的 2. 溫和的 3. 適度的，有節制的
ex: In more temperate regions, they may have to tolerate several months of winter, when subzero temperatures persist for long periods of time.
在溫帶地區，它們可能不得不忍受持續數月的冬季，在此期間零下氣溫會長時間持續。
deriv: temperately ad. 適度地，有節制地
words.en: having a mild climate; moderate

words.zh: 展望，設想
words.mnem: en- (=make) + vis (=see) + -ion → 展望，設想
ex: Recent progress in understanding Earth's early history indicates that both Oparin and Miller envisioned the atmospheric composition of early Earth.
近期在了解地球早期歷史方面取得的進展表明，Oparin 和 Miller 都曾設想過早期地球的大氣構成。
words.en: to imagine something in the future

words.zh: a. 完全的，十足的，徹底的；v. 說，發出，表達
ex: But whatever it was, it was worth it to them to spend hours deep inside a cave with just a torch between them and utter darkness.
但不管它是什麼，在洞穴深處待上幾個小時，僅靠一支火把置身於完全的黑暗中，這對他們來說都是值得的。
deriv: utterly ad. 完全地，徹底地
words.en: complete; to say something

words.zh: 地形的
words.mnem: topo (=place) + graph (=write) + -ical → 地形的
ex: The device had been much employed by topographical artists like the Italian painter Canaletto in his detailed views of the city of Venice.
這種設備已經為很多地形藝術家所用，像意大利畫家 Canaletto 就用它創作了精細的威尼斯城風景畫。
deriv: topographically ad. 從地形上，在地形構造方面
words.en: relating to the physical features of an area

words.zh: 石灰岩
ex: The limestone dissolves at a slow rate from acid rain.
石灰岩因酸雨而緩慢溶解。
words.en: a hard white rock containing calcium

words.zh: （尤指北美的）大草原
ex: The control of coyotes in the prairie region in the 1950s may have been a factor in raccoon expansion.
20 世紀 50 年代，草原地區對郊狼的控制可能是浣熊分佈範圍擴張的一個因素。
words.en: a large area of flat grassy land in North America

words.zh: 1. 使充滿，使飽和 2. 使濕透
words.mnem: satur (=enough) + -ate → 使飽和
ex: The termites saturate the atmosphere of the nest, bringing it to about 100 percent relative humidity, by carrying water up from the soil.
白蟻從土壤中向上輸送水分，使巢內的空氣飽和，相對濕度達到近 100%。
deriv: saturated a. 飽和的；浸透的
words.en: to fill something completely with liquid

words.zh: （尤指岩石的）裂縫，裂隙
ex: Now, other forms of life could take hold: ferns and mosses (two of the most ancient types of land plants) that flourish even in rock crevices.
現在，其他生命形式得以在此紮根：蕨類和蘚類植物（兩種最古老的陸生植物）甚至能在岩石縫隙中生長。
colloc: a crevice in a wall 牆上的裂縫
words.en: a narrow opening in a rock or wall

words.zh: 半乾旱的
ex: Well, shrub expansion has occurred in other environments, like semiarid grassland, and tall grass prairies.
灌木擴張已經出現在其他環境中，比如半乾旱草原和高草原。
words.en: having very little rain

words.zh: 人口稠密的，人口眾多的
words.mnem: popul (=people) + -ous → 人口稠密的
ex: It must be shipped 4,000 kilometers across the entire country to reach the populous East Coast.
它必須橫跨整個國家 4000 公里，才能送達人口密集的東海岸。
words.en: having a large population

words.zh: （岩石或土地的）裂縫，裂隙
ex: The organisms that inhabit cracks and fissures within the rocks are carried there by the groundwater flowing through them.
棲息在岩石裂縫和縫隙中的生物，是由流經這些地方的地下水輸送至此的。
colloc: a narrow fissure in rock 岩石上狹窄的裂縫
words.en: a long narrow crack

words.zh: 鵝卵石
ex: The male decorates the bower with feathers, flowers, pebbles, and shells.
雄鳥用羽毛、花朵、鵝卵石和貝殼來裝飾它的求偶亭。
colloc: not the only pebble on the beach 並非唯一要緊的人
words.en: a small smooth stone

words.zh: n. 孔隙；v.（~ over）認真研讀，鑽研
ex: The majority of petroleum is just filling in the tiny pores and cracks in rocks.
大部分石油只是填滿了岩石上的微小孔隙和裂縫。
deriv: porous a. 多孔的，有孔的
porosity n. 孔隙度，孔隙率
words.en: a very small hole in skin or rock

words.zh: 粉狀的
ex: Streak is the color of a mineral in its powdered form and is obtained by rubbing a mineral across a plate of unglazed porcelain.
條痕是礦物粉末的顏色，通過在無釉瓷板上摩擦礦物即可得到。
deriv: powder n. 粉末 v. 抹粉
words.en: in the form of powder

words.zh: 地圖繪製，製圖學
ex: The study of maps and cartography, the process by which they are made, can teach us about the geography of our planet and how people live in different regions.
研究地圖及地圖繪製過程，能幫助我們深入了解地球的地理特徵，以及各地域人們的生活方式。
words.en: the science of making maps

words.zh: （河流的）三角洲
ex: These fish lived in river channels and lakes on large deltas.
這些魚生活在大三角洲的河道和湖泊中。
words.en: the triangle-shaped area where a river meets the sea

words.zh: 沒有意識到的，不知道的
ex: Efforts to predict eruptions are thwarted, however, when we are unaware of a site's volcanic potential.
然而，當我們未意識到某地存在火山噴發風險時，火山噴發預測工作就會受阻。
deriv: awareness n. 認識，知道，意識
words.en: not knowing about something

words.zh: 1. 缺乏的，不足的 2. 少見的
ex: In desert environments, however, water is especially scarce.
然而，在沙漠環境中，水尤為稀缺。
deriv: scarcely ad. 幾乎不，簡直不
words.en: not enough in supply

words.zh: a. 1. 無規律的，不規則的 2. 不整齊的 3. 不正常的；n. 非正規軍軍人
ex: It creates irregular craters at low impact angles.
它會以低撞擊角度形成不規則的隕石坑。
deriv: irregularity n. 不規則，無規律
irregularly ad. 不整齊地，不規則地
words.en: not even or regular

words.zh: 宇航員
ex: A second problem is that astronauts on the Mars mission would be in the zero-gravity environment of space for many months at a time.
第二個問題是，執行火星任務的宇航員將在太空的零重力環境下一次待好幾個月。
words.en: a person trained to travel in space

words.zh: n. 塵土，粉塵；v. 1. 除去灰塵 2. 撒粉末於
ex: This dust cloud blocked the Sun's rays.
這片塵埃雲阻擋了太陽光線。
words.en: tiny dry pieces of earth or dirt

words.zh: 1. 相當地，一定地 2. 公正地，公平地
ex: Astronomers now have a fairly good idea of what a comet really is.
天文學家現在對彗星到底是什麼有了相當清晰的認識。
deriv: fair a. 合理的；公平的；相當大的
words.en: to a moderate degree; in a just way

words.zh: 樣本，樣品
ex: In this case, we can't predict the age with any accuracy unless we have actual samples from the planets.
在這種情況下，除非我們獲取這些行星的實際樣本，否則無法精確預測其年齡。
deriv: sampler n. 取樣器，取樣員
words.en: a small amount that shows what the whole is like

words.zh: a. 1. 液體的，液態的 2. 清澈的 3. 易變現的；n. 液體
ex: Liquid water could have formed on other planets as well.
液態水也可能在其他行星上形成。
words.en: a substance like water that flows

words.zh: 1. 鄰近地區，附近 2. 鄰里關係
ex: So it only spends about a year or two in our neighborhood, inside the orbit of Jupiter.
因此，它只在地球附近的木星軌道上運行一兩年時間。
colloc: in the neighborhood of 大約，左右
words.en: an area of a town; the area close to a place

words.zh: n. 尾巴，尾部；v. 跟蹤，尾隨
ex: When the comet gets even closer to the Sun, one of its most spectacular parts begins to form—the tail.
當彗星更加靠近太陽時，其最壯觀的部分之一——彗尾，便開始形成。
colloc: tail away 減少，逐漸消失
with one's tail between one's legs 夾著尾巴，垂頭喪氣
words.en: the part at the back of an animal; to follow someone secretly
syn: 追蹤，記錄（進展）2. 跟蹤

words.zh: a. 1. 固體的 2. 實心的 3. 結實的，穩定的；n. 固體
ex: Discovering new extraterrestrial water, whether past or present, liquid or solid, could significantly impact our understanding of life in the universe.
發現新的地外水——無論過去存在的還是現在存在的，是液態的還是固態的——都可能極大地影響我們對宇宙生命的認知。
deriv: solidarity n. 團結，齊心協力
words.en: hard and firm; not liquid or gas

words.zh: v. 1. 帶有，具有 2. 支持，支撐 3. 承受，忍受 4. 生產，生育 5. 開花，結果；n. 熊
ex: Altogether, roughly two tons of meteorite fragments were recovered, all of which bear the name Allende for the location of the first discovery.
人們總共找到了約兩噸的隕星碎片，所有的碎片均帶有 Allende 這一名稱，該名稱取自其首次發現地。
colloc: bear the responsibility 承擔責任
words.en: to carry or support; to tolerate; a large animal

words.zh: v. 1. 繪製地圖 2. 了解信息，提供信息；n. 地圖
ex: And he started keeping tracks of sunspots, mapping them, so he wouldn't confuse them with any potential new planet.
於是，他開始記錄太陽黑子的活動並繪製其分佈圖，以便不會將其與任何潛在的新行星混淆。
colloc: map out 在地圖上標出；籌劃
off the map 不重要的；不存在的；不易到達的
on the map 在地圖上；重要的；出名的
words.en: a drawing of an area; to make a map of something

words.zh: 小行星
ex: One possibility is from the impact of asteroids and comets on planets.
一種可能性是源於小行星和彗星對行星的撞擊。
words.en: a small rocky object that moves around the sun

words.zh: n. 1. 軌道 2. 影響範圍，勢力範圍；v. 繞軌道運行
ex: As the comet sweeps along its orbit, it leaves a curving trail of dust behind in its path.
當彗星沿著其軌道疾馳時，會在其運行路徑上留下一條彎曲的塵埃軌跡。
colloc: orbit the Earth 繞地球飛行
words.en: the curved path of an object around a planet or star

words.zh: a. 內部的，內在的；n. 裡面
ex: He theorized that comets form when passing stars push chunks of debris from the outer to the inner solar system.
他提出理論認為，當途經的恆星將碎片從外太陽系推至內太陽系時，彗星便形成了。
words.en: inside; closest to the center

words.zh: 天文學
ex: I might not have developed my interest in astronomy without that field trip experience.
如果沒有那次實地考察的經歷，我可能不會對天文學產生興趣。
deriv: astronomical a. 天文學的；極其巨大的
words.en: the scientific study of stars and planets

words.zh: 1. 可見的，看得見的 2. 明顯的
ex: Those impact craters are not visible on the Moon.
那些撞擊坑在月球上無法觀測到。
deriv: visual a. 視覺的，視力的
words.en: able to be seen

words.zh: 原子
ex: This collision causes the atoms to light up, to glow...different types of atoms glowing different colors.
這種碰撞會激發原子，使其發光……不同類型的原子發出不同的顏色。
words.en: the smallest unit of a chemical element

words.zh: 裸露的，赤裸裸的，無遮蔽的
ex: Most information about aurora intensity cannot be obtained through observation with the naked eye.
關於極光強度的大部分信息無法通過肉眼觀測獲得。
colloc: a naked hillside 光禿禿的山坡
words.en: not wearing clothes; without a covering

words.zh: 1. 使分佈，分散 2. 分銷 3. 分發，分配
ex: The craters are distributed randomly; they're all over the place, which is what we'd expect.
這些隕石坑呈隨機分佈，且遍佈各處，這正是我們預期的結果。
words.en: to give something out to several people

words.zh: v. [ter] 1. 撕裂，扯破 2. 流淚；n. [tɪr] 眼淚，淚水
ex: Rapidly, changes will begin to take place that will serve to tear the Sun apart.
很快，一系列變化將開始發生，這將導致太陽分裂。
colloc: tear at sth. 撕裂，扯開
tear sb./sth. away 使勉強離開；把……拿走
tear sth. down 拆毀，拆除
tear sb. apart 使不快，使擔心
tear sth. apart 撕毀，撕碎
words.en: to pull something apart; a drop of liquid from the eye

words.zh: 分類，歸類
ex: So Abell used categories like that to classify clusters on a scale: from regular to irregular.
因此，Abell 採用此類分類標準，按等級對星系團進行分類：從規則到不規則。
words.en: to arrange things into groups

words.zh: 1. 使命，任務 2. 代表團 3. 傳教，佈道
ex: Such findings could guide future missions in the search for habitable environments outside of Earth.
此類發現可為未來探測任務提供指導，助力尋找地球之外的宜居環境。
deriv: missionary a. 傳教的 n. 傳教士
words.en: an important task; a group of people sent to another country

words.zh: 1. 圍繞，包圍 2. 與……緊密相關
ex: So you end up with a solid core of rock, metal and ice surrounded by massive amounts of gas.
所以，最終會形成一個由岩石、金屬和冰構成的固體核心，其周圍環繞著大量氣體。
words.en: to be on all sides of something

words.zh: a. 1. 短暫的，簡短的 2. 簡潔的，簡單的；v. 給（某人）指示，向（某人）介紹情況；n. 摘要，概要
ex: The air friction can cause one of these bits of matter to produce a brief streak of light as it burns up in the atmosphere.
空氣摩擦會使這些物質碎片中的某一塊在大氣層中燃燒殆盡，同時產生一道短暫的光跡。
deriv: briefly ad. 簡要地，簡短地
words.en: short in time; short and simple

words.zh: 外面的，外部的，遠離中心的
ex: However, observations show that stars in the outer regions of galaxies rotate at unexpectedly high speeds.
然而，觀測結果表明，星系外圍區域的恆星正以出乎意料的高速度旋轉。
words.en: on the outside; far from the center

words.zh: n. 望遠鏡；v. 1.（使）套入，（使）嵌進 2. 縮短，精簡，壓縮
ex: Well, in optical astronomy, using a telescope and observing the stars that way, we rely on visible light waves.
在光學天文學領域中，當使用望遠鏡觀察星星時，我們依賴的是可見光波。
words.en: an instrument that makes distant things look nearer

words.zh: 輻射，放射線
ex: They observe cosmic microwave background radiation, the faint glow left over from the Big Bang, to gather information about the universe in its early days.
他們觀測宇宙微波背景輻射——即宇宙大爆炸留下的微弱餘暉，以此收集關於宇宙早期的信息。
words.en: energy sent out in the form of rays

words.zh: 天文學家
ex: It allowed astronomers to accurately measure the dimensions of stars.
它使天文學家能夠精確測量恆星的尺寸。
deriv: astronomical a. 天文學的；極其巨大的
words.en: a scientist who studies stars and planets

words.zh: 1.（尺寸、數量、規模）非常大的 2. 嚴重的
ex: This anomaly suggests that a type of massive, unseen matter is exerting gravitational force, keeping the stars moving faster than expected.
這種異常現象表明，存在一種大量的不可見物質正在施加引力，從而使恆星的運動速度比預期更快。
words.en: extremely large or heavy

words.zh: 巨大的，廣闊的，大量的
ex: The scope of this field is extremely large, encompassing everything from the smallest particles to vast galaxies.
該領域的研究範圍極其廣泛，涵蓋了從最小的粒子到巨大星系的一切事物。
words.en: extremely large in area or amount

words.zh: 1. 工具，儀器 2. 樂器
ex: Dark matter is a type of matter that doesn't emit, absorb, or reflect light, making it invisible to current instruments.
暗物質是一種不發射、吸收或反射光線的物質，這使其無法被現有儀器觀測到。
deriv: instrumental a. 起重要作用的；用樂器演奏的
words.en: a tool used for a task; a musical device

words.zh: 1. 宇宙 2. 領域，體系
ex: Dark matter is hugely important for the structure of the universe.
暗物質對宇宙結構而言至關重要。
deriv: universal a. 普遍的，全體的
words.en: all of space and everything in it

words.zh: 1. 星系 2. 群英
ex: Computer simulations show that galaxies wouldn't have formed the way they did if dark matter hadn't been around.
計算機模擬顯示，若不存在暗物質，星系就不會形成如今這般形態。
words.en: a very large group of stars

words.zh: 1. 碰撞 2. 衝突
words.mnem: col- (=together) + lide (=strike) → 碰撞；衝突
ex: Some of them make it into our upper atmosphere where they collide with atoms with oxygen and nitrogen atoms.
其中一些粒子進入高層大氣，在那裡與氧原子和氮原子發生碰撞。
words.en: to crash into something

words.zh: n. 1. 日食，月食 2. 黯然失色；v. 1. 遮住……的光 2. 使黯然失色
words.mnem: ec- (=out) + lipse (=leave) → 消失 → 日食，月食
ex: A coronagraph attaches to a telescope and acts like a disk that blocks out the Sun; it creates an artificial solar eclipse you could say.
日冕儀安裝在望遠鏡上，其作用就像一個能夠遮擋太陽的圓盤，可以說它製造了一場人造日食。
words.en: when the sun or moon is hidden by another body; to make something seem less important

words.zh: 星座
words.mnem: con- (=together) + stell (=star) + -ation → 星群 → 星座
ex: A couple weeks ago we looked at Castor, in the Gemini constellation.
幾周前，我們觀測了雙子座中的北河二。
words.en: a group of stars forming a pattern

words.zh: 碎片，殘骸
ex: And the debris from that collision could become part of the rings.
而且，此次碰撞產生的碎片可能成為（土星）環的一部分。
words.en: pieces left after something is destroyed

words.zh: n. 1. 刺眼的光 2. 怒視；v. 1. 發出刺眼的光 2. 怒視
ex: But this light is weaker than the glare of the moon's surface that we usually see when we observe the moon.
但這種光比我們平時觀測月亮時所看到的月球表面的強光更微弱。
words.en: a strong unpleasant light; to look angrily

words.zh: 彗星
ex: Comets lose matter each time they pass by the Sun, until they eventually disappear.
彗星每次經過太陽時都會損失物質，直至最終消失。
words.en: a bright object with a tail that moves around the sun

words.zh: a. 1. 爆炸的 2.（易）爆發的 3. 劇增的 4.（脾氣）暴躁的；n. 爆炸物，炸藥
words.mnem: ex- (=out) + plos (=clap) + -ive → 鼓掌，發出劇烈聲響 → 爆炸的
ex: Explosive impacts heated and liquefied the ice, resulting in the fluid appearance of the ejecta.
爆炸性的撞擊產生高溫將冰液化，導致噴出物呈現出流體狀的外觀。
words.en: able to explode; a substance that can explode

words.zh: v. 1. 開始，發起 2. 傳授，使了解 3. 接納新成員；n. 新入會的人
words.mnem: in- (=into) + iti (=go) + -ate → 走進入口 → 開始，著手
ex: For example, in 1989, there was a really intense magnetic storm initiated by a flare-up on the Sun, and it caused electricity to go out for 12 hours in Quebec, Canada.
例如，1989 年，太陽耀斑引發了一場非常強烈的磁暴，導致加拿大魁北克省的電力中斷了 12 小時。
deriv: initial a. 開始的，最初的 n. 首字母
words.en: to start something; to introduce someone to a group

words.zh: 1. 放大 2. 擴大，增強 3. 誇大
words.mnem: magn (=great) + -ify → 放大；擴大
ex: If you really magnify the spectrum of the sunlight, you could identify more than 100,000 of them.
如果充分放大太陽光譜，你就能識別出超過 10 萬條光譜線。
words.en: to make something look larger

words.zh: 1. 磁的，有磁性的 2. 富有吸引力的
ex: Let's start with solar activity and its interactions with Earth's magnetic field.
讓我們從太陽活動及其與地球磁場的相互作用開始講解。
words.en: having the power of a magnet; strongly attractive

words.zh: 1. 轟擊，轟炸 2. 連珠炮似地提問
ex: Earth's magnetic field is constantly being bombarded by charged particles.
地球磁場持續不斷地受到帶電粒子的轟擊。
words.en: to attack with bombs; to send a lot of things at someone

words.zh: 1. 帶電的 2. 飽含激情的
ex: Sunspots emit charged particles that collide with atoms in Earth's upper atmosphere.
太陽黑子會釋放帶電粒子，這些帶電粒子會與地球高層大氣中的原子發生碰撞。
deriv: charge v. 充電；收費；指控 n. 電荷；收費；指控
chargeable a. 應徵稅的；應支付的
words.en: having an electrical charge; full of strong emotion

words.zh: 1. 使……嵌入（埋入）2. 使根深蒂固
ex: It consists mainly of ices (water, methane, ammonia) with bits of dust embedded in it.
它主要由冰（水、甲烷、氨）構成，裡面嵌有少量塵埃。
colloc: be embedded in sth. 嵌在／埋在某物中
words.en: to fix something firmly into a surface

words.zh: a. 1. 微弱的，模糊的 2. 虛弱暈眩的，無力的；v. 昏厥；n. 昏厥
ex: One problem is that radio waves from these faraway objects are extremely faint.
一個問題是，來自這些遙遠天體的無線電波極其微弱。
colloc: in a (dead) faint（完全）失去知覺
words.en: not strong or clear; to lose consciousness

words.zh: 1. 跳躍，飛躍 2. 激增，猛漲
ex: So, it's really not much of a leap to theorize that a good number of them might have ended up on the moon.
所以，理論上推斷其中相當一部分最終可能落在了月球上，這並非太大跳躍的推斷。
words.en: to jump high or far; a sudden increase

words.zh: 月亮的，月球的
ex: Some estimates hold that there may be a million tons of helium-3 buried on the lunar surface.
據估算，月球表面可能埋藏著 100 萬噸氦-3。
words.en: relating to the moon

words.zh: 1. 強度，烈度 2. 強烈，劇烈
words.mnem: in- (=toward) + tens (=stretch) + -ity → 拉伸至緊繃的狀態 → 強度；強烈
ex: It is incorrect to claim that sunspots increase the intensity of Earth's magnetic field at the poles.
聲稱太陽黑子會增強地球兩極的磁場強度，這一說法是不正確的。
colloc: grow in intensity 愈演愈烈
deriv: intense a. 強烈的，劇烈的
tense a. 緊張的；緊繃的 v. 使緊張；使緊繃
words.en: the strength of something

words.zh: 1. 運用，施加 2. 竭力，努力
words.mnem: ex- (=out) + ert (=put) → 向外施展 → 運用，施加
ex: That's because magnetic fields reduce the pressure exerted on the gases inside of them, making the spots cooler than the rest of the Sun's surface.
那是因為磁場降低了施加在其內部的氣壓，使得黑點比太陽表面其他區域的溫度更低。
colloc: exert an influence on 對……產生影響
words.en: to use power or influence; to make a great effort

words.zh: 1. 縮小，收縮，皺縮 2. 逃避，退縮
ex: The core will shrink, giving off the last of its energy, and the Sun will finally die.
地核會收縮，釋放出最後殘存的能量，太陽最終會消亡。
colloc: shrink from sth./doing sth. 不願做某事
words.en: to become smaller

words.zh: v. 剝去，剝奪；n. 條，帶，條狀物
ex: The one on the upper right has been stripped of gas and dust, which is one clear sign that there has been a collision.
右上角的那個（星系）已被剝離了氣體和塵埃，這是發生過碰撞的一個明顯跡象。
words.en: to remove something from a surface; a long narrow piece

words.zh: v. 盤旋上升（或下降）；a. 螺旋的；n. 1. 螺旋形 2. 盤旋上升（或下降）
ex: Then we believed they gradually spiral down out of the rings and into the planet's atmosphere.
當時我們認為，它們逐漸螺旋下降，脫離了行星環，並進入行星大氣層。
words.en: a curve winding around a center

words.zh: 流星
ex: This streaking phenomenon is called a meteor.
這種劃過天際的現象被稱為流星。
words.en: a bright streak of light in the sky from a falling space rock

words.zh: 1. 宇宙的 2. 巨大且重要的
words.mnem: cosm (=universe) + -ic → 宇宙的
ex: Yes, and there's extreme temperatures, cosmic rays, ultraviolet radiation.
沒錯，（太空中）存在極端溫度、宇宙射線和紫外線輻射。
words.en: relating to the universe

words.zh: 消失，滅絕
words.mnem: van (=empty) + -ish → 空的 → 消失，滅絕
ex: Where do the new comets come from to replace the old ones that dissipate and vanish from view?
新彗星從何而來，以取代那些消散並從視野中消失的舊彗星呢？
words.en: to disappear suddenly

words.zh: 1. 碰撞 2. 衝突，抵觸
words.mnem: col- (=together) + lis (=strike) + -ion → 碰撞；衝突
ex: The only other possibility is that we are seeing results of shock waves produced by the collision of these two galaxies.
唯一的另一種可能性是，我們看到的是這兩個星系碰撞產生的衝擊波引發的結果。
words.en: a crash between moving objects

words.zh: 在……之下
words.mnem: be- (=by) + neath (=down) → 在……之下
ex: Mars' subsurface shows evidence of water beneath it.
火星地表下層顯示出其下方存在水的證據。
words.en: under; at a lower level

words.zh: 1.（使）旋轉，（使）轉動 2.（人員）輪換，輪值
words.mnem: rot (=turn) + -ate →（使）旋轉，（使）轉動
ex: All the stars in a galaxy rotate around the center of their galaxy.
星系中的所有恆星都圍繞其星系中心旋轉。
colloc: rotate about/around sth. 繞著……旋轉
words.en: to turn around a central point

words.zh: 軌道的
ex: A planet's original orbital path can change surprisingly quickly.
一顆行星的原始軌道可能會以驚人的速度發生改變。
deriv: orbit v. 沿軌道運行 n. 軌道
words.en: relating to the path of an object around a planet

words.zh: v.（使）打旋，旋動；n. 1. 旋動，打旋 2. 螺旋形，旋渦形
ex: As the disk kept swirling around, bits of matter collided, and some stuck together in clumps.
隨著圓盤持續旋轉，物質微粒相互碰撞，其中一些微粒聚集成團塊。
words.en: to move quickly in circles

words.zh: （使）同步
words.mnem: syn- (=same) + chron (=time) + -ize → 時間一致 →（使）同步
ex: We need to get all those components to work together, to synchronize, so the light from all the different telescopes reaches the computers at exactly the same time.
我們需要使所有這些組件協同工作、保持同步，從而讓來自不同望遠鏡的光信號能夠完全同時送達計算機。
deriv: synchronous a. 同步的，共時的
words.en: to happen or operate at the same time

words.zh: （事業、理論等的）支持者，擁護者
words.mnem: pro- (=before) + pon (=put) + -ent → 在前面的人 → 支持者，擁護者
ex: But then you also have proponents of the meteorite theory.
但與此同時，也存在隕石理論的支持者。
words.en: a person who supports an idea or plan

words.zh: n. 邊緣；v. 構成……的邊緣
ex: For example, large quantities of meteoric iron were identified around the crater rim and on the surrounding plain.
例如，在該隕石坑邊緣及周邊平原上，已經發現了大量隕鐵。
words.en: the edge of something round

words.zh: a. 1. 缺乏的，沒有……的 2. 無效的 3. 空的；n. 1. 空間，空白 2. 空虛；v. 1. 正式宣布……無效 2. 排放
ex: However, unlike Jupiter, the terrestrial planets today are nearly void of light gases and ices.
然而，與木星不同的是，如今類地行星上的輕質氣體和冰極度缺乏。
colloc: be void of 沒有，缺乏
deriv: voidable a. 可以作廢的，可使無效的
words.en: empty; having no legal force

words.zh: 1. 多石頭的 2. 冷漠的，無情的
ex: I mean, it's easier to find an iron meteorite or stony iron.
我的意思是，鐵隕石或石鐵隕石更容易被發現。
words.en: full of stones; cold and unfriendly

words.zh: 使變形
words.mnem: de- (=away) + form (=form) → 使變形
ex: Ice on Callisto does not deform or flow like ice in glaciers on Earth.
木衛四上的冰不會像地球冰川中的冰那樣發生變形或流動。
deriv: deformed a. 變形的，畸形的
words.en: to change the shape of something so it looks worse

words.zh: 天空的，天上的
words.mnem: celest (=sky) + -ial → 天空的，天上的
ex: Just think about all those tools we've discussed—celestial bodies, magnetic fields, landmarks—they've got a lot of sensory cues at their disposal.
想想我們討論過的那些工具——天體、磁場、地標——它們擁有大量可供利用的感官線索。
words.en: relating to the sky or heaven

words.zh: 1. 不對稱的 2. 不平衡的
ex: Maybe a particular sunspot was sort of square, then later it would become more lopsided, then later something else.
也許某個特定的太陽黑子起初近似方形，之後變得愈發不對稱，再之後又會變成其他形狀。
deriv: lopsidedness n. 不勻稱；不平衡
words.en: not balanced; with one side higher or heavier

words.zh: 行星的
ex: On a solid planet with a hydrosphere and an atmosphere, only a tiny fraction of the planetary mass flows as surface fluids.
在一顆擁有水圈和大氣層的固態行星上，僅有極小一部分行星質量以表面流體的形式流動。
words.en: relating to planets

words.zh: 1. 天頂 2. 頂點，最高點，巔峰
ex: One important way the Polynesians had for orienting themselves was by using zenith stars.
波利尼西亞人確定方位的一種重要方法是觀察天頂星。
words.en: the highest point; the point in the sky directly above you

words.zh: 一大片，廣闊，寬廣
words.mnem: ex- (=out) + pans (=spread) + -e → 向外延伸的部分 → 一大片，廣闊，寬廣
ex: Other researchers go even further, suggesting that the data provide evidence for large open expanses of water on the early Martian surface.
其他研究人員更進一步提出，這些數據為早期火星表面存在大面積廣闊水域提供了證據。
words.en: a wide open area

words.zh: 盛行的，流行的
words.mnem: pre- (=excessively) + vail (=strong) + -ing → 盛行的
ex: Over the years, the prevailing belief that lunar craters were formed by volcanic activity was challenged by proponents of the meteor impact theory of crater formation.
多年來，認為月球隕石坑是由火山活動形成的主流觀點，受到了隕石撞擊坑理論支持者的挑戰。
colloc: a prevailing practice 流行慣例
deriv: prevail v. 流行，盛行；戰勝，壓倒
words.en: most common or widespread

words.zh: 辨別，看出，覺察出
words.mnem: dis- (=apart) + cern (=separate) → 辨別
ex: So it was easier to discern the order in the sky than farther north or farther south, where everything would seem more chaotic.
所以，相比一切看似更混亂的靠北和靠南的地方，（赤道）這裡更容易辨認出天空中的星序。
deriv: discernment n. 辨別（力），洞察力
words.en: to see or understand something with difficulty

words.zh: 太陽黑子
ex: The biggest magnetic disturbances coincided with dramatic auroras, and also with the timing of the most intense sunspot activity.
最強烈的磁擾與壯觀的極光同時出現，也與最劇烈的太陽黑子活動時間相吻合。
words.en: a dark area on the sun's surface

words.zh: 1. 摩擦，摩擦力 2. 爭執，分歧
ex: The air friction can cause one of these bits of matter to produce a brief streak of light as it burns up in the atmosphere.
空氣摩擦會使這些物質碎片中的某一塊在大氣層中燃燒殆盡，同時產生一道短暫的光跡。
words.en: the force that resists sliding; disagreement

words.zh: （使）噴出，（使）湧出
ex: The force of collision spewed large amounts of debris into the atmosphere, darkening the skies for several years before the finer particles settled.
撞擊產生的衝擊力將大量碎片噴入大氣層，導致天空昏暗了數年之久，直至這些小顆粒沉降為止。
words.en: to flow out in large amounts

words.zh: 引力的
words.mnem: grav (=heavy) + it + -ation + -al → 引力的
ex: The gravitational influence of a passing star can be sufficient to perturb the orbit of one of these chunks.
一顆經過的恆星產生的引力影響，足以擾亂這些天體碎塊中某一塊的軌道。
words.en: relating to the force of gravity

words.zh: 速度，速率
words.mnem: veloc (=fast) + -ity → 速度
ex: The particles enter Earth's atmosphere at high velocity.
這些粒子以高速進入地球大氣層。
words.en: speed in a particular direction

words.zh: （距離或時間的）接近，鄰近
words.mnem: proxim (=near) + -ity → 接近
ex: The type of tail exhibited by a comet depends on its proximity to the Sun.
彗星呈現的尾部形態取決於它與太陽的距離。
colloc: in close proximity 非常靠近的，緊挨的
words.en: nearness in space or time

words.zh: 巨大的，龐大的
ex: This forms a gigantic halo around the ice ball.
這在冰球周圍形成了一個巨大的光環。
words.en: extremely large

words.zh: 1. 橢圓的 2. 隱晦的
ex: Under the control of the Sun's gravitational force, each planet maintains an elliptical orbit.
由於太陽引力的作用，每顆行星都在橢圓軌道上運行。
words.en: shaped like an oval

words.zh: 各種各樣
words.mnem: as- (=to) + sort (=kind) + -ment → 各種各樣
ex: When broken open, Allende stones are revealed to contain an assortment of small, distinctive objects.
當阿倫德隕石被剖開時，人們發現其內部含有多種小巧而獨特的物體。
colloc: a mixed assortment of sweets 什錦糖果
deriv: assorted a. 各種各樣的，什錦的
words.en: a mixed group of different things

words.zh: 重新分配
words.mnem: re- (=again) + dis- (=apart) + tribut (=bestow) + -e → 重新分配
ex: You know planetary researchers love studying deep craters to learn about the impacts that created them, how they redistributed pieces of a planet's crust.
要知道，行星研究者們熱衷於研究深隕石坑，以了解形成這些深坑的衝擊力，以及這些衝擊力是如何重新分佈行星地殼碎片的。
words.en: to share something out in a different way

words.zh: 行星間的
ex: What's especially interesting about meteoroids is that they come from interplanetary space.
流星體尤其有趣的一點，在於它們來自行星際空間。
words.en: between planets

words.zh: 天文館
ex: To test the idea, caged night-migrating birds were placed on the floor of a planetarium during their migratory period.
為了證實這個觀點，研究人員在鳥類遷徙期間，把籠養的夜間遷徙鳥類放置於天文館的地面上。
words.en: a building with a dome that shows the stars

words.zh: 宇宙學家
words.mnem: cosmo (=universe) + log (=study) + -ist → 宇宙學家
ex: Cosmologists also study dark matter and dark energy.
宇宙學家還致力於研究暗物質與暗能量。
words.en: a scientist who studies the origin of the universe

words.zh: 天文台，天文觀測站，氣象台
words.mnem: ob- (=to) + serv (=keep) + -atory → 保持專注力，用於觀測的場所 → 天文台，天文觀測站，氣象台
ex: Some archaeological evidence indicates it could be constructed by the same people who built the famous astronomical observatory site, Stonehenge, in Great Britain.
一些考古證據表明，它可能是由建造英國著名天文觀測遺址（巨石陣）的同一批人所建。
deriv: observer n. 觀察者；評論員
observe v. 觀察；遵守；評論；慶祝
words.en: a building for observing the stars
